title.narrative: Consolidation Phase Linking Agriculture with Natural Resource Management and Nutrition (LANN+) & Covid-19 Response

description.narrative: The community based LANN(Linking Agricultural and Natural Resource Management Towards Nutrition Security ) component targets women groups and their households in rural chiefdoms (Koya in Kenema, and Kunike and Kunike-Barina in Tonkolili). The target communities are home to some of the country's most vulnerable households, located in remote, rural communities in forested area in Kenema, the targeted chiefdom is located adjacent to the Gola Rainforest National Park. These households primarily depend on subsistence agriculture with limited access to market and cash income opportunities, especially in Kenema where bigger periodic markets are scarce in the chiefdom. Furthermore, access to social infrastructure (e.g. education and health) is likewise a challenge. In Koya chiefdom there are 06 Peripheral Health Units (PHUs) serving the targeted communities, and also 06 PHUs serving the target communities in Kunike and Kunike-Barina chiefdoms in Tonkolili.

The project is a 1 year follow up consolidation phase with a COVID-19 modifier to the 3 year Linking Agriculture with Natural Recourse Management and Nutrition (LANN) project implemented previously The key LANN pillar activities are finally consolidated while groups' independence and initiative is strengthened for them to develop and implement their own priority projects. Coordination and sector learning is supported to through the engagement of the Scaling Up Nutrition and Immunization (SUNI) platforms and sector partners.Responding to COVID-19, through raising awareness and promoting preventive measures in the targeted communities; strengthening community resilience to mitigate negative impacts on Food and Nutrition Security FNS; while supporting the health actors through contact tracing, mobilization and more adequate treatment facilities.

The proposed project aims to contribute to its overall purpose through interventions with the aim of leading to the following objectives : Improved diversity and quality of the household diet, with a specific focus on improved child-feeding practices and dietary diversity for children under five in targeted communities; Enhanced ability of vulnerable households to improve Food and Nutrition Security; Improved hygiene, sanitation and access to safe drinking water leading to reduced prevalence of diarrhea among young children; Enhanced inter-sectorial learning and coordination on Food and; Nutrition Security at district and national level;COVID-19 preparedness, prevention and resilience strengthened and negative impacts on FNS mitigated in the targeted communities.
